---
applyTo: "**/src/test/munit/**/*.xml,**/src/test/resources/**"
---

# MUnit changes

Follow the project's existing suite conventions first; these rules fill gaps and prevent false passes. Consult the documentation for the project's MUnit version; links below are MUnit 3.6 examples, and 3.7 changes assertion-error behavior.

## Correctness

- Read the project's MUnit version, suite layout, reusable fixtures, and existing assertions first. Use supported processors and matchers for that version. Organize preparation, invocation, and validation using the established MUnit pattern. See [MUnit test structure](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/munit-test-concept).
- Assert observable behavior, not merely that the flow ran: payload shape/value, required attributes or variables, output/error contract, and meaningful side effects. Treat every flow and subflow you change as an interface: at least one test supplies its inputs and asserts its outputs. Include happy, boundary, and expected-failure paths affected by the change, with one test for each Choice route and each error path.
- Isolate real external I/O at a narrow, identifiable boundary. Match the intended processor and distinguishing attributes, and include a readable one such as `doc:name` rather than `doc:id` alone, which tells a reviewer nothing about what is replaced; ensure a mock does not accidentally intercept unrelated calls. Assert important call counts when behavior depends on them. See [Mock When](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/mock-event-processor) and [Verify Call](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/verify-event-processor).
- Assert request-building values with a `before` spy on the connector, then establish how they bind to its body, headers, query/URI parameters, method/path, and configuration by reviewing that processor's parameter expressions. MUnit mock/verify matching targets processor attributes such as `method` or `config-ref`; do not invent assertions on resolved connector internals. When the resolved request itself must be observed, use an approved local stub integration test. A correct mock response can hide a wrong request.
- Keep the business logic real; do not bypass or replace the main business transform to obtain a green test. A spy observes event state; its payload/attribute/variable changes do not persist to the original event. Pair required observations with an executed exact or minimum call check: `atMost` permits zero. Consult [Spy](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/spy-event-processor) and [Verify Call](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/verify-event-processor).
- Distinguish expected propagated errors from handled responses. Propagation can skip `munit:validation`; do not put required assertions there and assume they ran. If post-error checks are needed, use version-supported test-only capture of the specific expected error type, record that it occurred, fail if no error occurred, then execute the assertions and call checks. Never let a handler that could match assertion or `verify-call` failures wrap them: from MUnit 3.7.0 assertion failures are catchable `MUNIT-TOOLS:ASSERTION_ERROR` errors. A swallowed error is not a pass. Keep production propagation unchanged. See [error testing](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/test-mock-errors-cookbook).
- Mock errors supported by modules in the tested flow; unsupported types can become `MULE:UNKNOWN`. Verify the intended mapping. For `target`/`targetValue`, assert the stored result and preserved event as appropriate; the payload may still be the old input. When mocking that processor, define the target variable with the expected result shape. Review the actual target binding separately: a variable supplied by the mock does not prove that binding. See [target-variable testing](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/test-processor-that-uses-target-variable).
- Tests must be deterministic and safe: no live production calls, fixed synthetic inputs, controlled time-dependent behavior, and no secrets. Control `now()`, UUIDs and random values by mocking the Set Variable that produces them and returning fixed variables; if they are generated inside a Transform, report that the flow needs that small change rather than asserting around changing values. Mocks apply after app initialization; some connectors still need valid test configuration. Transform Message and Logger processors cannot be mocked. Report blockers rather than adding real credentials. See [mock limitations](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/mock-event-processor).
- Do not assume `equalTo` ignores object-key order. Prefer stable field/invariant assertions or deliberately normalize only contract-irrelevant ordering. See [comparable matchers](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/comparable-matchers-reference).
- A direct `flow-ref` test does not prove HTTP transport status, TLS, gateway policies, or deployment behavior. Enable event sources only for an intentional integration test. See [flow sources](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/enable-flow-sources-concept).

## Practices

- Test one behavior per `munit:test`. Give it a `name` and `description` that state the scenario and expected outcome, and keep suites organized the way the project already does (for example one suite per flow or API resource). With no existing convention, a readable `<flow>_<condition>_<expectedOutcome>` name is a reasonable default.
- Supply what the flow actually reads with `munit:set-event`: payload with its media type, plus the attributes and variables the flow uses (for example HTTP query parameters when a listener flow is called through `flow-ref`), and nothing it does not read. Inputs and assertions that trace to no requirement or contract are noise: they make later readers wonder what matters.
- Keep inputs, expected outputs and mock responses as sanitized files under `src/test/resources` and load them with `readUrl('classpath://...')` or `MunitTools::getResourceAsString`, instead of large inline payloads. See [mocking with files](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/mock-file-cookbook).
- Compare the whole contract-relevant result rather than one convenient field or `notNullValue`. Use `MunitTools` matchers with `munit-tools:assert-that`, or `dw::test::Asserts` matchers with `munit-tools:assert`/`munit-tools:that`; these matcher APIs are not interchangeable. See [Assert Expression](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/assertion-expression-processor) and [DataWeave assertions](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/dataweave-assertions-library).
- Use parameterized suites (`munit:parameterizations`) when the same scenario runs over several inputs, instead of copied tests; each case still needs assertions that distinguish it. See [parameterized suites](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/parameterized).
- Put shared setup in `before-suite`/`before-test` and clean it up in the matching `after-*` scope. Tests must not depend on execution order or on another test's side effects. Stateful components such as Round Robin keep their position between calls; account for it so each test exercises the intended route. See [before and after scopes](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/before-after-scopes-reference).
- Bind any local listener or stub port with `munit:dynamic-port` so suites can run in parallel and in CI. Keep test-only property values in the project's test properties; never point tests at a real environment. See [dynamic ports](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/dynamic-ports).
- Tag slow or integration tests with `tags` and select them with `-Dmunit.tags` or `-Dmunit.test`. Tests that do not match a selection, or carry `ignore="true"`, are reported as ignored; read that count, and do not leave a test ignored without a recorded reason. See [MUnit Maven plugin](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/munit-maven-plugin).
- Coverage is diagnostic; high coverage without useful assertions is not sufficient. Keep any configured coverage thresholds (`requiredApplicationCoverage` and similar) and never lower them to make a build pass; do not introduce a new numeric target copied from a tutorial without a team decision. Write the tests that check contracts first, then use coverage to find untested paths. Suites scaffolded by the Studio Test Recorder still need review before they count: trim recorded payloads and mocks to the fields the flow uses, give generated files meaningful names and the real media type where the project allows it, remove assertions on time-dependent or random values, and write error-path tests by hand, because the recorder cannot record flows that raise errors. See [Test Recorder](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/test-recorder). See [coverage in Maven](https://docs.mulesoft.com/munit/3.6/coverage-maven-concept).
- Do not trust a test you have not seen fail. When tests can be run, confirm each new test fails against a deliberately wrong expected value or behavior, then restore it; report the check, or say it was not done.
- Run the repository's targeted and required aggregate test commands. Report executed, ignored and failed counts from actual output.
